summary.text: Milankovitch cycles are the combined effects on Earth's climate, over thousands of years, of slow changes in the way Earth moves.
The main changes are in the shape of the orbit, the tilt of Earth's axis and the direction the axis points, which together shift how much sunlight reaches each place and season.
These changes come from the gravity of other bodies in the Solar System, with Jupiter and Saturn mainly driving changes in the orbit's shape.

facts.label: Northern seasons
facts.value: Summer runs 4.66 days longer than winter

items.prompt: Suppose Earth's axis leaned over more steeply than it does today. What would happen to the seasons?

options.label: They would become milder
They would become more extreme
They would stay exactly the same
They would swap between hemispheres

items.explain: A greater tilt of Earth's axis makes the seasons more extreme.

items.prompt: Earth passes closest to the Sun in early January. Which season is the Northern Hemisphere in at that moment?

options.label: Summer
Spring
Winter
Autumn

items.explain: Closest approach falls around 3 January, during northern winter, so distance from the Sun is not what makes the seasons.

items.prompt: Earth moves fastest near its closest point to the Sun, which it now reaches in January. In the Northern Hemisphere, how do summer and winter compare in length?

options.label: Winter is longer, since Earth is nearer the Sun
They are equal, since seasons are fixed quarters
Winter is longer, since Earth moves slowly then
Summer is longer, since Earth moves slowly then

items.explain: Earth races through the January part of its orbit, shortening northern winter, and moves slowly near its farthest point, so northern summer is 4.66 days longer.

items.prompt: Milanković paid special attention to sunlight changes at 65° north. Why that latitude?

options.label: It holds a great amount of land, which heats and cools quickly
It gets more sunlight than any other latitude
It is mostly ocean, which stores heat for a long time
It is where the tilt of the axis is measured

items.explain: He stressed 65° north because of its great amount of land, and land changes surface temperature more quickly than ocean.

items.prompt: An orbital change slowly raises the sunlight reaching two regions, one mostly land and one mostly ocean. Why does the ocean region's surface warm more slowly?

options.label: Seawater reflects nearly all sunlight back to space
Mixing with deeper water keeps the surface cooler
Salt in seawater stops it absorbing any heat
Ocean regions receive less sunlight than land

items.explain: Mixing between shallow and deeper water keeps the ocean surface relatively cool, so oceans change temperature more slowly than land.

items.prompt: Over a long cycle, Earth's orbit stretches from nearly round to more oval. What happens to the length of the year?

options.label: It gets longer as the orbit stretches
It gets shorter as the orbit stretches
It changes by a few days each century
It stays the same throughout

items.explain: The orbit's semi-major axis does not change, and the length of the year is set by that axis, so the year stays the same.
